MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT DETAILS
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Fetal tissue (uncultured solid tissue)
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL DETAILS
Reason for Referral: Analysis of fetal tissue
Clinical Information: Advanced maternal age

TEST PERFORMED
Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA) for all chromosome subtelomere regions
Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured solid fetal tissue using standard protocols. MLPA analysis was performed using SALSA MLPA probemix P036 and P070 for human telomere screening, covering all subtelomeric regions. The analysis was carried out according to manufacturer's instructions (MRC-Holland). QF-PCR was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. Fragment analysis was performed on an Applied Biosystems 3730xl DNA Analyzer.

RESULTS

MLPA ANALYSIS - SUBTELOMERE REGIONS
All subtelomeric regions tested: NORMAL
No copy number imbalances detected in any subtelomeric region
Dosage quotient values within normal range (0.80-1.20) for all probes

QF-PCR ANALYSIS
Chromosome 13: Two alleles detected - Normal disomic pattern
Chromosome 18: Two alleles detected - Normal disomic pattern
Chromosome 21: Two alleles detected - Normal disomic pattern
Chromosome X: Two alleles detected
Chromosome Y: No Y-specific products detected
Sex chromosome complement: Consistent with female (XX)

No evidence of triploidy detected
No evidence of whole chromosome aneuploidy for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X or Y

INTERPRETATION
No abnormality detected. The results show no imbalance in the tested subtelomeric regions and no aneuploidy for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X or Y. The findings are consistent with a normal female sex chromosome complement. There is no evidence of triploidy, whole chromosome aneuploidy, or subtelomere imbalance in the regions tested.

LIMITATIONS
This test will not detect:
- Balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Small intrachromosomal imbalances (<200kb at subtelomeres)
- Mosaicism below the level of approximately 20-30%
- Maternal cell contamination below detectable levels
- Abnormalities in regions not covered by the MLPA probes
- Point mutations or small insertions/deletions

The absence of maternal cell contamination cannot be completely excluded without comparative maternal sample analysis.

CONCLUSION
Normal female genetic profile without chromosomal abnormalities in the regions tested.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorised by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Scientist
